content.thinking:
The test is slow (the reference DP with a full g-table computed via ref_g for all 4096 pairs is O(4096 × n) with n up to 60 → 245k ref_g calls each O(n)... that's very slow). It got through the 60 tight cases (18 feasible, 42 infeasible) in ~180s and then timed out during the broad sweep.

Interesting: 42 of 60 tight cases were infeasible — my solver agreed with the reference on all of them (both feasibility and optimality) ✓.

Let me make the broad sweep lighter (fewer cases, smaller FIBs) and run it separately to completion.

arguments.command:
cd /app/tmp && python3 - << 'EOF'
p='/app/tmp/test_final.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("""# broad random sweep
for trial in range(120):
    style = ['deep', 'shallow', 'mixed', 'clustered'][trial % 4]
    n = rng.randint(0, 120)""",
"""# broad random sweep
for trial in range(50):
    style = ['deep', 'shallow', 'mixed', 'clustered'][trial % 4]
    n = rng.randint(0, 40)""")
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF
cd /app/tmp && timeout 175 python3 test_final.py 2>&1 | tail -3
